newsitem.title: USA: ARCO Q3 earnings up 52pct on crude, natgas.
newsitem.headline: ARCO Q3 earnings up 52pct on crude, natgas.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) said Monday its third quarter earnings rose 52 percent on higher crude oil prices, natural gas production and improved refining operations.
Third quarter earnings rose to $479 million, or $2.94 per share, compared with 1995 third quarter earnings of $315 million, or $1.93 per share.

"ARCO's oil and natural gas operations benefited from higher prices and growing natural gas production to give us a 146 percent increase in earnings from this segment," Mike Bowlin, ARCO's chairman, said in a statement.
Natural gas production grew by about 20 percent compared to last year, led by a 38 percent increase in overseas gas production, Bowlin said.
Earnings for West Coast refining and marketing rose 77 percent, with sales volumes of light product up five percent.
"All of these factors, combined with our lowered cost structure, gave ARCO excellent results in the third quarter," Bowlin said.
Net income for the first nine months of 1996 grew to $1.283 billion, or $7.86 per share, up 25 percent from $1.028 billion, or $6.29 per share, in the same period of 1995.

Overseas, ARCO began joint venture production from the Rhourde El Baguel field in Algeria in the third quarter. It also signed an agreement to produce and upgrade heavy oil in Venezuela, pending government approval.
Domestically, ARCO plans to start production at the new Alpine field in Alaska's Western Colville area by 2000.
ARCO said earnings from its West Coast refining operations totaled $133 million after tax, up from $75 million in the 1995 third quarter.
The company said the improved performance resulted from strong products prices and increased volumes, which offset higher crude costs.
Gasoline, jet fuel and diesel margins were all stronger than a year ago, with jet fuel demand particularly strong, the company said.
